---
title: Configuration
description: Every environment variable Renplay reads, with its default.
---

<!-- Generated by docs/site/scripts/gen-config.mjs from server/src/envvars.ts. Do not edit by hand. -->

Renplay works without any configuration. These environment variables are for special setups. Set
them on the container, for example with `-e RENPLAY_IMAGE_QUALITY=80` or in the `environment:`
block of a Compose file.

A variable that is empty counts as not set. The container runs as any non-root user and with a
read-only root filesystem, so any folder you point a variable at must be writable by that user.

## Folders

<div class="config-entry" id="games-dir">

**`GAMES_DIR`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: `/games`

</div>

Where installed games live. Put this on a big disk.

</div>

<div class="config-entry" id="data-dir">

**`DATA_DIR`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: `/data`

</div>

Saves and their history, the library database, mods, covers and walkthroughs. Use a local disk, never a network share: SQLite needs local filesystem locking. Back this up.

</div>

<div class="config-entry" id="archives-dir">

**`ARCHIVES_DIR`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: `/downloads` if it exists and is writable, otherwise `$GAMES_DIR/_archives`

</div>

Downloads and the drop folder (zip, 7z, rar), kept for reinstalls. An explicit path overrides automatic detection. Existing files are never moved.

</div>

<div class="config-entry" id="renplay-dir">

**`RENPLAY_DIR`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: `$GAMES_DIR/_renplay`

</div>

Engines and scratch space. Keep it on the same filesystem as `GAMES_DIR`.

</div>

<div class="config-entry" id="saves-dir">

**`SAVES_DIR`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: `$DATA_DIR/saves`

</div>

Where saves are stored, laid out like desktop Ren’Py does.

</div>

<div class="config-entry" id="save-history-dir">

**`SAVE_HISTORY_DIR`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: `$DATA_DIR/save-history`

</div>

Earlier versions of saves that were overwritten or deleted.

</div>

<div class="config-entry" id="overlays-dir">

**`OVERLAYS_DIR`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: `$DATA_DIR/overlays`

</div>

Mods: your files, layered over a game.

</div>


## Games and catalog

<div class="config-entry" id="renplay-adult-default">

**`RENPLAY_ADULT_DEFAULT`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: `off`

</div>

Ceiling and starting choice of adult games for newly created accounts: off, blurred or shown (allow and block work as before). The first admin always starts at shown. Admins can change the ceiling per account in Users.

</div>

<div class="config-entry" id="renplay-keep-downloads">

**`RENPLAY_KEEP_DOWNLOADS`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: `true`

</div>

Keep downloads after install so games can be reinstalled. `false` deletes only unchanged uploads through Renplay after a successful install. Files copied in are never deleted automatically. Setting this variable locks the Settings switch. When unset, admins can choose in Settings.

</div>

<div class="config-entry" id="renplay-delete-archives">

**`RENPLAY_DELETE_ARCHIVES`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: not set

</div>

Deprecated alias for the opposite of `RENPLAY_KEEP_DOWNLOADS`. `true` deletes uploaded downloads and `false` keeps them. Still supported in 3.x, with a warning once at startup. `RENPLAY_KEEP_DOWNLOADS` takes precedence when both are set.

</div>

<div class="config-entry" id="renplay-adult-games">

**`RENPLAY_ADULT_GAMES`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: not set

</div>

The installation level of adult games: off (they do not exist), blurred (they show with hidden art) or shown, and the choice is fixed. The 3.x spellings work too: allow is shown, block is off. Not set: the stored choice applies (shown until an install answers its first-run question), and admins can change it in Settings. At off the server reads the catalog’s safe-for-work index. Below shown it never downloads adult art. Any other value counts as off.

</div>

<div class="config-entry" id="renplay-catalog-urls">

**`RENPLAY_CATALOG_URLS`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: `https://catalog.renplay.org/index.v4.json`

</div>

Catalog indexes, separated by commas. The first one that defines a tag wins. Schema 4 indexes give each game its pictures in five formats. A schema 3 index still works, its cover becoming the grid.

</div>

<div class="config-entry" id="renplay-engines-url">

**`RENPLAY_ENGINES_URL`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: `https://engines.renplay.org/index.json`

</div>

Where the Ren’Py web engines come from.

</div>

<div class="config-entry" id="renplay-engine">

**`RENPLAY_ENGINE`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: newest for the game

</div>

Build every game with this one engine version, such as one the engines index lists. A game’s recipe still wins.

</div>

<div class="config-entry" id="renplay-recipes-dir">

**`RENPLAY_RECIPES_DIR`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: recipes in the data folder

</div>

Your recipes: a folder of recipe files in the catalog’s format, read as one more catalog. A recipe here takes the place of a catalog recipe with the same id.

</div>


## Images and saves

<div class="config-entry" id="renplay-image-quality">

**`RENPLAY_IMAGE_QUALITY`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: `88`

</div>

WebP quality (1 to 100) for converted images.

</div>

<div class="config-entry" id="renplay-image-concurrency">

**`RENPLAY_IMAGE_CONCURRENCY`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: CPU count (at most 16)

</div>

Images converted in parallel during an install. `0` picks the CPU count.

</div>

<div class="config-entry" id="renplay-save-history">

**`RENPLAY_SAVE_HISTORY`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: `20`

</div>

Earlier versions kept per save file.

</div>

<div class="config-entry" id="renplay-backup-dir">

**`RENPLAY_BACKUP_DIR`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: backups/saves in the data folder

</div>

Where a daily zip of everyone’s saves goes. Point it at another disk or a share to keep a copy apart from the data folder. `off` turns save backups off. A server that sleeps when idle makes the backup the next time it runs.

</div>

<div class="config-entry" id="renplay-sync-server">

**`RENPLAY_SYNC_SERVER`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: `https://sync.renpy.org`

</div>

The Ren’Py sync server for Sync codes, which an admin turns on in Settings. Change it only to use your own server that speaks the same protocol.

</div>

<div class="config-entry" id="renplay-backup-keep">

**`RENPLAY_BACKUP_KEEP`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: `14`

</div>

Save backups kept. Older ones are deleted.

</div>


## Behind a proxy

<div class="config-entry" id="renplay-public-url">

**`RENPLAY_PUBLIC_URL`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: not set

</div>

Public address, such as https://play.example.org. Used to check request origins and secure cookies. Plain HTTP works too, but HTTPS protects passwords and saves in transit.

</div>

<div class="config-entry" id="renplay-trusted-hops">

**`RENPLAY_TRUSTED_HOPS`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: `1`

</div>

Trusted proxy hops for client addresses and HTTPS detection. The included nginx is one hop. Use 0 when exposing Node directly; never trust arbitrary forwarded headers.

</div>

<div class="config-entry" id="renplay-keepalive-url">

**`RENPLAY_KEEPALIVE_URL`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: not set

</div>

For scale-to-zero setups: a public URL that routes back to this server. While an install runs, Renplay keeps requesting it so the proxy does not stop the server.

</div>

<div class="config-entry" id="renplay-keepalive-host">

**`RENPLAY_KEEPALIVE_HOST`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: not set

</div>

The `Host` header to send with the keep-alive requests, if the proxy routes by host name.

</div>


## Server

<div class="config-entry" id="puid">

**`PUID`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: `1000`

</div>

Container only: when started as root, drop to this non-root user ID before starting Renplay. Ignored when started with --user. Make the mounted folders writable by this user; Renplay does not change their ownership.

</div>

<div class="config-entry" id="pgid">

**`PGID`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: `1000`

</div>

Container only: group ID to use with PUID when started as root. Ignored when started with --user.

</div>

<div class="config-entry" id="renplay-oidc-issuer">

**`RENPLAY_OIDC_ISSUER`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: empty

</div>

OIDC issuer URL. Enables discovery and single sign-on. Requires HTTPS, except loopback test servers.

</div>

<div class="config-entry" id="renplay-oidc-client-id">

**`RENPLAY_OIDC_CLIENT_ID`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: empty

</div>

OIDC client id. Register /api/auth/oidc/callback on RENPLAY_PUBLIC_URL as the callback URL.

</div>

<div class="config-entry" id="renplay-oidc-client-secret">

**`RENPLAY_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: empty

</div>

OIDC client secret. Prefer the _FILE variant. Empty supports public clients with PKCE.

</div>

<div class="config-entry" id="renplay-oidc-client-secret-file">

**`RENPLAY_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET_FILE`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: empty

</div>

Read the OIDC client secret from this file. Set this or RENPLAY_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET, not both.

</div>

<div class="config-entry" id="renplay-oidc-name">

**`RENPLAY_OIDC_NAME`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: `Single sign-on`

</div>

Name on the sign-in and account buttons.

</div>

<div class="config-entry" id="renplay-oidc-auto-create">

**`RENPLAY_OIDC_AUTO_CREATE`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: `true`

</div>

Create accounts at first OIDC sign-in. If false, people must explicitly link their identity while signed in first.

</div>

<div class="config-entry" id="renplay-oidc-admin-group">

**`RENPLAY_OIDC_ADMIN_GROUP`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: empty

</div>

Exact groups claim value granting Admin. Provider grants follow membership at each OIDC sign-in, even for the last admin. Admin access assigned in Users is kept.

</div>

<div class="config-entry" id="renplay-oidc-adult-group">

**`RENPLAY_OIDC_ADULT_GROUP`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: empty

</div>

Deprecated alias of RENPLAY_OIDC_ADULT_GROUPS: the group gets shown, everyone else off. Still supported, with a warning once at startup. RENPLAY_OIDC_ADULT_GROUPS takes precedence when both are set.

</div>

<div class="config-entry" id="renplay-oidc-adult-groups">

**`RENPLAY_OIDC_ADULT_GROUPS`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: empty

</div>

Adult games ceilings by sign-in group: group=off, =blurred or =shown, separated by commas. Matches the groups claim exactly. When set, a person’s ceiling is the highest level of their groups, or off when none match, recomputed at each OIDC sign-in, and Users cannot change it.

</div>

<div class="config-entry" id="renplay-admins">

**`RENPLAY_ADMINS`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: empty

</div>

Comma-separated provider usernames or verified OIDC emails granted Admin when no admin group/filter is configured. Grants are checked at each sign-in and removed on unlink. Admin access assigned in Users is kept. LDAP email is not treated as verified.

</div>

<div class="config-entry" id="renplay-ldap-url">

**`RENPLAY_LDAP_URL`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: empty

</div>

LDAP directory URL, ldap:// or ldaps://. Prefer TLS. Enables directory password sign-in.

</div>

<div class="config-entry" id="renplay-ldap-bind-dn">

**`RENPLAY_LDAP_BIND_DN`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: empty

</div>

Directory service account DN used to search for users and check groups.

</div>

<div class="config-entry" id="renplay-ldap-bind-password">

**`RENPLAY_LDAP_BIND_PASSWORD`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: empty

</div>

Directory service account password. Prefer the _FILE variant.

</div>

<div class="config-entry" id="renplay-ldap-bind-password-file">

**`RENPLAY_LDAP_BIND_PASSWORD_FILE`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: empty

</div>

Read the LDAP bind password from this file. Set this or RENPLAY_LDAP_BIND_PASSWORD, not both.

</div>

<div class="config-entry" id="renplay-ldap-base-dn">

**`RENPLAY_LDAP_BASE_DN`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: empty

</div>

Base DN under which user entries are searched.

</div>

<div class="config-entry" id="renplay-ldap-user-filter">

**`RENPLAY_LDAP_USER_FILTER`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: `(&(objectClass=person)(uid={username}))`

</div>

User search filter. Every {username} is escaped before substitution. Exactly one entry must match.

</div>

<div class="config-entry" id="renplay-ldap-username-attribute">

**`RENPLAY_LDAP_USERNAME_ATTRIBUTE`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: `uid`

</div>

Directory attribute for the username.

</div>

<div class="config-entry" id="renplay-ldap-name-attribute">

**`RENPLAY_LDAP_NAME_ATTRIBUTE`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: `displayName`

</div>

Directory display-name attribute; falls back to cn, then username.

</div>

<div class="config-entry" id="renplay-ldap-email-attribute">

**`RENPLAY_LDAP_EMAIL_ATTRIBUTE`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: `mail`

</div>

Directory email attribute. LDAP email never grants admin access through RENPLAY_ADMINS.

</div>

<div class="config-entry" id="renplay-ldap-photo-attribute">

**`RENPLAY_LDAP_PHOTO_ATTRIBUTE`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: `jpegPhoto`

</div>

Directory binary photo attribute, copied locally at sign-in.

</div>

<div class="config-entry" id="renplay-ldap-admin-filter">

**`RENPLAY_LDAP_ADMIN_FILTER`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: empty

</div>

Filter evaluated against the authenticated user entry, such as memberOf=cn=renplay-admins,ou=groups,dc=example,dc=org. Provider grants follow membership at each LDAP sign-in, even for the last admin. Admin access assigned in Users is kept.

</div>

<div class="config-entry" id="renplay-ldap-adult-filter">

**`RENPLAY_LDAP_ADULT_FILTER`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: empty

</div>

Deprecated alias of RENPLAY_LDAP_ADULT_GROUPS: a matching entry gets shown, everyone else off. Filter evaluated against the authenticated user entry at each LDAP sign-in. RENPLAY_LDAP_ADULT_GROUPS takes precedence when both are set.

</div>

<div class="config-entry" id="renplay-ldap-adult-groups">

**`RENPLAY_LDAP_ADULT_GROUPS`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: empty

</div>

Adult games ceilings by directory group: group=off, =blurred or =shown, separated by commas. Matches the cn of the user’s memberOf groups, case-insensitive. When set, the ceiling is the highest level of their groups, or off when none match, recomputed at each LDAP sign-in, and Users cannot change it.

</div>

<div class="config-entry" id="renplay-ldap-starttls">

**`RENPLAY_LDAP_STARTTLS`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: `false`

</div>

Require StartTLS before sending any credentials over ldap://. A failed TLS upgrade refuses sign-in.

</div>

<div class="config-entry" id="renplay-ldap-ca-file">

**`RENPLAY_LDAP_CA_FILE`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: empty

</div>

PEM CA certificate file for directory TLS. Certificate verification is always enabled.

</div>

<div class="config-entry" id="renplay-auth">

**`RENPLAY_AUTH`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: on for new installs, off after an upgrade

</div>

`on` requires sign-in. `off` lets everyone play as one account. Saves always stay separate per account. Upgraded installs show an admin reminder while sign-in is off.

</div>

<div class="config-entry" id="renplay-auth-user">

**`RENPLAY_AUTH_USER`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: `1`

</div>

Account id used without sign-in. The owner is 1; other accounts and their saves stay untouched.

</div>

<div class="config-entry" id="renplay-auth-local">

**`RENPLAY_AUTH_LOCAL`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: `true`

</div>

Enable username and password sign-in. With sign-in on, disabling the only provider refuses startup.

</div>

<div class="config-entry" id="renplay-admin-username">

**`RENPLAY_ADMIN_USERNAME`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: not set

</div>

Claim the owner account at first start with this username and RENPLAY_ADMIN_PASSWORD. Otherwise use the setup code printed in the server log.

</div>

<div class="config-entry" id="renplay-admin-password">

**`RENPLAY_ADMIN_PASSWORD`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: not set

</div>

Initial owner password (at least 10 characters). Only used while the owner is unclaimed. Prefer RENPLAY_ADMIN_PASSWORD_FILE.

</div>

<div class="config-entry" id="renplay-admin-password-file">

**`RENPLAY_ADMIN_PASSWORD_FILE`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: not set

</div>

Read the initial owner password from this secret file. Set this or RENPLAY_ADMIN_PASSWORD, not both.

</div>

<div class="config-entry" id="port">

**`PORT`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: `3000`

</div>

Port of the Renplay server inside the container. nginx listens on 8080 and forwards to it, so you rarely change this.

</div>

<div class="config-entry" id="renplay-log-level">

**`RENPLAY_LOG_LEVEL`**

<div class="config-default">

Default: `info`

</div>

How much the server logs. `error`: errors only. `warn`: also warnings and requests that failed on the server. `info`: also the start summary, installs, catalog updates, backups, sign-ins, and requests that change something or fail. `debug`: every request and each install as it runs.

</div>


## Folders inside the container

| Folder | What is in it |
|---|---|
| `/data` | Saves and their history, accounts, the SQLite library, mods, covers, walkthroughs. **Local disk only. Back this up.** |
| `/downloads` | Optional downloads and drop folder. Used when it exists and is writable, or when selected with `ARCHIVES_DIR`. Downloads are kept by default. `RENPLAY_KEEP_DOWNLOADS=false` deletes only unchanged completed uploads after a successful install. Files copied in are never deleted automatically. |
| `/games/_archives` | Downloads when no usable `/downloads` exists. Existing files are never moved. |
| `/games` (the rest) | Installed games, engines and scratch space. Scratch stays on this filesystem for atomic installs. Rebuilding requires the original downloads. |

Deleting `/data` loses saves and the library. Deleting `/games` also loses downloads stored
inside it. Deleting a download means reinstalling needs that download again. Settings shows
the downloads folder in use.
